sources.title: International Boundary Study No. 42: Burma–China Boundary
sources.issuer: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Intelligence and Research, Office of the Geographer
sources.archive: Florida State University College of Law, archived government-issued study; not a present-day government-hosted treaty original
locators: Appendix printed 18: Articles VII(3), VIII, X
sources.findings: Northern description names Nmai/Irrawaddy, Salween, Tulung/Taron and Tsayul watersheds, Western Chingdam, Tusehpong/Kundam Razi, Yulang and Gamlang passes. Article VII(3) cites 1:250,000 whole-boundary and 1:50,000 selected-area treaty maps. Article X makes later protocol maps replacements. Printed 9 says protocol text and large-scale maps were not public as of 1964.
sources.limits: Actual treaty/protocol annex maps are absent from this 20-page archive PDF. Northern sheet numbers, datum, coordinates and township correspondence are not supplied. Historical availability is not a claim about availability today. Shared drainage names provide geographic relevance only, without exact candidate registration.

sources.title: International Boundary Study No. 80: Burma–India Boundary
sources.issuer: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Intelligence and Research, Office of the Geographer
sources.archive: Florida State University College of Law, archived government-issued study
locators: Printed 2: 1967 agreement background and quoted delimitation begins
Printed 8: Treaty D and Summary IV
sources.findings: Reproduces delimitation of agreement signed Rangoon 10 March 1967. Northern description reaches Shawngshan Bum, then follows Irrawaddy–Brahmaputra watershed; exact northern extremity remains provisional pending final determination. Summary identifies annexed 1:126,720 strip maps. Demarcation was separate future work as of publication.
sources.limits: Actual strip-map annexes are absent from this 10-page archive PDF. Northern sheet identifiers, datum, survey control and current terminus determination not established. Southern Survey of India sheet footnotes are not evidence for this northern group.

concrete_blocker: The accessible government-issued primary texts identify the required map annex scales and replacement protocol but do not contain the actual annex map sheets. No presently retrievable official 1961 protocol map set, northern 1967 strip sheet, datum/control definition, later northern-terminus determination or 2019 township crosswalk was established. Those exact documents are needed before registration to original ADM3 geometry or candidate cells could be assessed.
